To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the subjective mood estimation co-varied with spectral power EEG parameters, 2) the co-variation between mood and EEG parameters was frequency- and localization-dependent, and 3) the co-variability was different for two mood dimensions: Energy and Tension.
the subjective estimation of mood is co-varied with the EEG spectral power parameters, which is a novel finding.
subjective estimation of Energy correlates negatively with alpha1 relative power and positively with delta and theta1 relative power.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of the relation of subjective mood estimation and objective brain characteristics.
the relationship between subjective estimation of mood and EEG parameters.
the co-variations between subjective estimation of mood and spectral power EEG characteristics, which may be used as objective correlates of mood.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the brain correlates of the mood dimensions are not only in the frequency domain, but they are also in the localization domain, and that the localization is not necessarily restricted to the fronto-central areas.
the EEG correlates of mood are not simple, and that they depend upon the specific mood dimensions, and their specific poles.
the EEG characteristics, which were used, do not reflect mood in a simple way, but rather that they are involved in its regulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

subjective estimation of mood is related to the spectral power characteristics of EEG, which is consistent with the view that subjective mood is a result of brain activity, and not only a result of external stimuli or a result of the subjects' expectations.
the EEG is a valid measure of subjective mood, and the subjective mood can be a useful measure of brain activity, as reflected by EEG.
the brain is a complex system, which is able to process and store information about the environment and the organism itself, and that the information processing is reflected in the EEG.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the subjective mood estimation co-varied in a specific manner with the spectral power EEG characteristics.
the subjective estimation of mood has a specific EEG signature.
the subjective experience of energy, and of tension, is reflected in EEG spectral characteristics.
